stories.body: UN climate talks in Turkey ended Sunday without adopting their main political agreement after the EU, UK, small island states and other countries rejected a text that omitted any explicit mention of fossil fuels. Poorer countries also objected to the lack of concrete adaptation-finance commitments, including a baseline for measuring last year's pledge to triple funding. Oil-producing countries had resisted stronger fossil-fuel language. Delegates approved some separate decisions, including measures on a just transition for workers, but the failure to agree on the central text exposed deep divisions over emissions cuts and who should pay for climate adaptation.
stories.headline: COP31 ends without a main climate agreement after fossil-fuel and finance disputes

stories.body: Iran has intensified attacks on tankers and US military positions amid an American naval blockade and sanctions campaign. Al Jazeera reported about 25 tanker incidents in and around the Strait of Hormuz over the past week, sharply reducing oil flows through a passage that normally carries roughly a fifth of global oil and gas. British maritime authorities reported two tankers struck by unidentified projectiles near Oman. Iran's Revolutionary Guards also claimed to have destroyed US air-defense radars in Bahrain; those claims were not independently established in the supplied reporting. US Central Command denied a separate Iranian claim that it had damaged an American F-16.
stories.headline: Iran escalates Gulf attacks as tanker strikes disrupt Hormuz shipping

stories.body: The Russian navy corvette Merkury sank after a suspected sea-drone attack in Benghazi early Sunday, with satellite imagery showing most of the vessel submerged. A Russia-linked commercial vessel was hit off the port later that day, and injured crew members were rescued. Local officials attributed the warship attack to Ukrainian drones, but no one claimed responsibility and Russia had not immediately commented. The strikes suggest a further expansion of attacks on Russian maritime operations beyond the Black Sea. Libya's eastern administration condemned the attacks as violations of its sovereignty, while the UN mission called for an independent investigation.
stories.headline: Russian warship sinks after suspected Ukrainian drone attack in Libya

stories.body: Ukrainian officials said ten people were killed when a Russian strike destroyed part of an apartment building in Dymer, north of Kyiv, early Sunday, updating initial reports of two deaths. Rescuers pulled a seven-year-old boy out alive after 14 hours and also saved a 79-year-old woman. Separate strikes killed one person in Bila Tserkva and three at a grocery store in Vyshneve, where 13 people were wounded. Rescue operations continued despite repeated air-raid alerts. Ukraine's interior minister reported more than 70 strikes across ten regions by Sunday evening.
stories.headline: Russian strike kills ten in Dymer as rescuers pull a child from the rubble

stories.body: British food businesses welcomed an agreement intended to remove most checks on food, plants and animal products traded with the EU and reopen markets for products including fresh sausages, seed potatoes and molluscs. Implementation is scheduled for March 1, 2028, and some producers say rebuilding lost trade will take longer: Scottish seed-potato growers may need years to revive varieties previously sold in Ireland. Prime Minister Andy Burnham is due to defend the wider EU agreement in Parliament Monday, citing a Treasury estimate of up to £17 billion in economic benefits. Opponents dispute that estimate and object to Britain following EU rules.
stories.headline: UK-EU food deal promises fewer border checks, with implementation set for 2028

stories.body: Rescuers were preparing to resume searches Monday at a confectionery factory near Jakarta after a Saturday fire killed at least three people and left dozens unaccounted for. Police had recovered 24 body bags by Sunday evening but cautioned that these did not establish a death toll because individual bags could contain remains from more than one person. The factory's latest statement listed 29 workers missing and another eight whose whereabouts were unconfirmed. Identification will require DNA testing and could take two to three weeks. Remaining hotspots and the risk of structural collapse have complicated searches; the cause remains under investigation.
stories.headline: Dozens missing after Indonesian factory fire; recovered remains await identification

stories.body: Education Minister Choi Kyo-jin resigned after criticism of last-minute security measures for South Korea's university entrance exam, taken by about 500,000 students Thursday. The scramble followed a confession by the top scorer in a separate tax-accountancy exam that he had used a concealed camera, smartphone and AI to answer questions. Authorities sent nationwide emergency phone alerts to expose hidden devices, inspected eyewear and covered clothing buttons to block cameras. The ministry said 111 entrance-exam candidates were found with unauthorized smart devices. President Lee Jae Myung accepted Choi's resignation after the minister acknowledged inadequate preparation.
stories.headline: South Korea's education minister resigns after scramble to prevent AI exam cheating

stories.body: Democrat Chuck Hubbard defeated longtime Republican Representative Virginia Foxx in North Carolina's fifth district after a recount, winning by 330 votes with 99% counted. The result brings Democrats to at least 258 House seats, matching their 1992 total, against at least 173 for Republicans, with four contests unresolved. Democrats also won control of the Senate. The incoming majorities will strengthen their ability to investigate the Trump administration and block nominations, although legislation will still face a presidential veto. Hubbard emphasized living costs during the Iran war and said Foxx had conceded and committed to a smooth transition.
stories.headline: North Carolina recount gives Democrats at least 258 House seats

stories.body: The US Army says it can use an emergency exemption to detonate more than four tonnes of unstable lead azide at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant despite a federal appeals court's stay of its permit. Government lawyers argue that approaching freezing temperatures increase the risk of an uncontrolled explosion and say action is needed by Tuesday; state health officials listed two planned blasts for Monday. Environmental groups challenging the operation say authorities failed to assess safer alternatives or adequately prepare residents for potential lead contamination. The legal dispute now turns partly on whether the claimed exemption allows the Army to proceed independently of the suspended permit.
stories.headline: Army invokes emergency powers to pursue Iowa explosives detonation despite court stay

stories.body: Falling trees and a streetlight injured twelve people across Catalunya Sunday, two seriously. Nine participants in Barcelona's Cursa de les Dones suffered minor injuries when a tree fell on Avinguda Meridiana; another person was seriously injured by a falling tree at Parc de Carles I. A driver in Matadepera was also seriously hurt, and a falling streetlight injured someone in Sabadell. Barcelona firefighters handled more than 100 wind-related incidents by early afternoon. City officials said the race continued because keeping runners together was considered safer and the level-three weather alert did not require cancellation.
stories.headline: Windstorm injures twelve across Catalunya, including nine Barcelona runners

stories.body: Christmas-light preparations will close sections of Passeig de Gràcia's central roadway from 10 a.m. Monday through Thursday: toward the sea between Diagonal and Provença, and uphill between Aragó and Diagonal. Side lanes initially remain open. Thursday's lighting ceremony expands the closure to the entire stretch between Diagonal and Gran Via from 2 p.m., with nearby metro entrances closing from 5 p.m. Bus routes 22 and 24 in both directions, and 7 and V15 uphill, will be diverted until 8 a.m. Friday. Bicing station 374 is also closed until Friday morning; alternative metro stations for the ceremony include Catalunya, Fontana and Verdaguer.
stories.headline: Passeig de Gràcia closures and bus diversions begin Monday
